name: Data Structures & Algorithms
description: DSA interview preparation covering fundamental data structures, problem-solving patterns, and algorithmic techniques.

subTopics.name: Prefix Sum
subTopics.description: Use cumulative sums to efficiently calculate subarray sums and solve range and exact-sum problems.

subTopics.name: Prefix Sum Fundamentals
subTopics.description: Build cumulative sums and use prefix sums to calculate subarray sums efficiently.

subTopics.name: Prefix Sum with HashMap
subTopics.description: Use prefix sums with a HashMap to solve exact subarray sum problems, including cases containing negative numbers.

subTopics.name: Binary Search
subTopics.description: Use binary search to efficiently search sorted data and monotonic answer spaces.

subTopics.name: Binary Search Fundamentals
subTopics.description: Search for an element in a sorted array using left, right, and middle pointers.

subTopics.name: Binary Search on Answer
subTopics.description: Apply binary search to a monotonic search space when the answer itself is not directly present in the array.

subTopics.name: Heap / Priority Queue
subTopics.description: Heap fundamentals, PriorityQueue operations, Top-K patterns, custom comparators, and advanced heap problems.

subTopics.name: Heap Fundamentals
subTopics.description: Min Heap, Max Heap, peek, add, poll, and heap time complexity.

subTopics.name: Top K Pattern
subTopics.description: Kth Largest, Kth Smallest, keeping K largest or smallest elements using heaps.

subTopics.name: Kth Largest
subTopics.description: Find the Kth largest element using a Min Heap of size K.

subTopics.name: Kth Smallest
subTopics.description: Find the Kth smallest element using a Max Heap of size K.

subTopics.name: Top K Frequent Elements
subTopics.description: Use a frequency HashMap and Min Heap of size K with custom comparator and tie-breaking.

subTopics.name: Custom Heap Comparator
subTopics.description: Design custom PriorityQueue comparators using frequency, distance, and tie-breaking rules to keep the worst candidate at the root.

subTopics.name: K Closest Elements
subTopics.description: Keep K elements with the smallest distance from a target using a Max Heap where the farthest element is the worst candidate.

subTopics.name: K Closest Points
subTopics.description: Use a Max Heap of size K based on x² + y² where the farthest point is the worst candidate and is removed first.

subTopics.name: Merge K Sorted Lists
subTopics.description: Use a Min Heap containing one current element from each sorted list and insert the next element from the list after polling.

subTopics.name: Kth Largest in Stream
subTopics.description: Maintain a Min Heap of size K while processing streaming values.

subTopics.name: Median From Data Stream
subTopics.description: Use two heaps: Max Heap for the smaller half and Min Heap for the larger half while maintaining balanced heap sizes.

subTopics.name: Sliding Window
subTopics.description: Solve contiguous subarray and substring problems by maintaining and efficiently updating a window.

subTopics.name: Fixed Size Sliding Window
subTopics.description: Maintain a window of fixed size and update the result when the window moves.

subTopics.name: Maximum Sum Subarray of Size K
subTopics.description: Maintain the sum of a fixed-size window by adding the incoming element and removing the outgoing element.

subTopics.name: Maximum Average Subarray
subTopics.description: Find the maximum average of a fixed-size subarray by maintaining the maximum window sum.

subTopics.name: First Negative Number
subTopics.description: Track indexes of negative numbers using a queue to find the first negative number in every fixed-size window.

subTopics.name: Maximum Vowels in Substring
subTopics.description: Maintain the number of vowels in a fixed-size substring by adding the incoming character and removing the outgoing character.

subTopics.name: Variable Size Sliding Window
subTopics.description: Expand and shrink a dynamic window based on a validity condition to find optimal subarrays or substrings.

subTopics.name: Minimum Subarray Length
subTopics.description: Find the minimum-length contiguous subarray whose sum is at least a target using window expansion and contraction.

subTopics.name: Longest Subarray with Constraint
subTopics.description: Find the longest valid subarray by expanding the right pointer and shrinking from the left when the constraint is violated.

subTopics.name: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
subTopics.description: Use a HashSet and sliding window to maintain a substring containing only unique characters.

subTopics.name: At Most K Distinct Characters
subTopics.description: Use a frequency HashMap to find the longest substring containing at most K distinct characters.

subTopics.name: Longest Subarray with At Most K Odd Numbers
subTopics.description: Maintain the count of odd numbers and find the longest contiguous subarray containing at most K odd numbers.

subTopics.name: Longest Subarray with Sum Less Than Target
subTopics.description: For positive integers, maintain a variable window whose sum remains strictly less than the target.

subTopics.name: Sliding Window with Frequency Map
subTopics.description: Use HashMap frequency tracking to maintain character or element counts inside the current window.

subTopics.name: Character Replacement
subTopics.description: Find the longest substring that can be converted into one repeated character using at most K replacements. Required replacements are window size minus maximum frequency.

subTopics.name: Minimum Window with Required Characters
subTopics.description: Find the minimum substring containing all required characters by tracking their frequencies and shrinking a valid window.

subTopics.name: Longest / Shortest Window
subTopics.description: Find the longest or shortest valid contiguous subarray or substring using window expansion and contraction.

subTopics.name: Minimum Length Window
subTopics.description: Once a window becomes valid, repeatedly shrink it to find the smallest possible valid window.

subTopics.name: Maximum Length Window
subTopics.description: Maintain a valid window and update the maximum length whenever the current window satisfies the constraint.

subTopics.name: Counting with Sliding Window
subTopics.description: Count all valid contiguous subarrays by using the current valid window length to determine how many valid subarrays end at the right pointer.

subTopics.name: Count Subarrays with Sum at Most K
subTopics.description: For positive integers, count subarrays with sum less than or equal to K using count += right - left + 1 after restoring window validity.

subTopics.name: Count Subarrays with Product Less Than K
subTopics.description: For positive integers, maintain a product-based sliding window and count valid subarrays using the current window length.

subTopics.name: Sliding Window Pattern Recognition
subTopics.description: Identify when Sliding Window applies and distinguish it from techniques such as Prefix Sum when negative numbers make window behavior unpredictable.

subTopics.name: Two Pointers
subTopics.description: Solve array and string problems using two indices that move based on the problem conditions.

subTopics.name: Opposite Direction Two Pointers
subTopics.description: Start pointers from both ends and move them toward each other based on comparisons or constraints.

subTopics.name: Same Direction Two Pointers
subTopics.description: Use two pointers moving through the array or string at different positions to maintain a valid range.

subTopics.name: Sorted Array Two Pointers
subTopics.description: Use the sorted order to efficiently find pairs or combinations satisfying a target condition.

subTopics.name: Fast and Slow Pointers
subTopics.description: Use pointers moving at different speeds for cycle detection, finding the middle, and related linked-list patterns.

name: System Design
description: Comprehensive study guide covering Low-Level Design (LLD) and High-Level Design (HLD).

subTopics.name: Low-Level Design (LLD) / Object-Oriented Design
subTopics.description: Focuses on classes, objects, interfaces, and design patterns.

subTopics.name: Design Principles (SOLID)
subTopics.description: Core object-oriented design principles to build maintainable, flexible, and scalable software systems.

subTopics.name: Single Responsibility Principle (SRP)
subTopics.description: A class should have only one reason to change, meaning it should perform only a single job or module responsibility.

subTopics.name: Open/Closed Principle (OCP)
subTopics.description: Software entities should be open for extension, but closed for modification.

subTopics.name: Liskov Substitution Principle (LSP)
subTopics.description: Subtypes must be substitutable for their base types without altering the correctness of the program.

subTopics.name: Interface Segregation Principle (ISP)
subTopics.description: Clients should not be forced to depend upon interfaces and methods they do not use.

subTopics.name: Dependency Inversion Principle (DIP)
subTopics.description: High-level modules should depend on abstractions rather than low-level modules and concrete implementations.

subTopics.name: Design Patterns (Gang of GoF)
subTopics.description: Standard reusable solutions to common software design problems in enterprise systems.

subTopics.name: Creational Patterns
subTopics.description: Mechanisms that deal with object creation mechanisms to increase flexibility and reuse of existing code.

subTopics.name: Singleton Pattern
subTopics.description: Ensure a class has only one instance and provide a global point of access to it.

subTopics.name: Factory Method Pattern
subTopics.description: Define an interface for creating an object, but let subclasses decide which class to instantiate.

subTopics.name: Abstract Factory Pattern
subTopics.description: Provide an interface for creating families of related or dependent objects without specifying concrete classes.

subTopics.name: Builder Pattern
subTopics.description: Separate the construction of a complex object from its representation so that the same construction process can create different representations.

subTopics.name: Prototype Pattern
subTopics.description: Specify the kinds of objects to create using a prototypical instance, and create new objects by copying this prototype.

subTopics.name: Structural Patterns
subTopics.description: Mechanisms that explain how to assemble objects and classes into larger structures while keeping them flexible and efficient.

subTopics.name: Adapter Pattern
subTopics.description: Convert the interface of a class into another interface clients expect, allowing incompatible interfaces to work together.

subTopics.name: Decorator Pattern
subTopics.description: Attach additional responsibilities to an object dynamically to provide a flexible alternative to subclassing.

subTopics.name: Facade Pattern
subTopics.description: Provide a unified interface to a set of interfaces in a subsystem to make the subsystem easier to use.

subTopics.name: Composite Pattern
subTopics.description: Compose objects into tree structures to represent part-whole hierarchies, allowing clients to treat individual objects and compositions uniformly.

subTopics.name: Proxy Pattern
subTopics.description: Provide a surrogate or placeholder for another object to control access to it.

subTopics.name: Behavioral Patterns
subTopics.description: Mechanisms that deal with algorithms and the assignment of responsibilities between objects.

subTopics.name: Observer Pattern
subTopics.description: Define a one-to-many dependency between objects so that when one object changes state, all its dependents are notified automatically.

subTopics.name: Strategy Pattern
subTopics.description: Define a family of algorithms, encapsulate each one, and make them interchangeable at runtime.

subTopics.name: Command Pattern
subTopics.description: Encapsulate a request as an object, thereby letting you parameterize clients with different requests, queue or log requests, and support undoable operations.

subTopics.name: State Pattern
subTopics.description: Allow an object to alter its behavior when its internal state changes, appearing to change its class.

subTopics.name: High-Level Design (HLD) / System Architecture
subTopics.description: Focuses on system architecture, databases, scaling, and network protocols.

subTopics.name: Architectural Patterns
subTopics.description: High-level architectural patterns for modern distributed and scalable systems.

subTopics.name: Microservices Architecture
subTopics.description: Decomposing applications into small, loosely coupled, independently deployable services.

subTopics.name: Event-Driven Architecture
subTopics.description: Asynchronous communication and workflow management driven by event generation and consumption.

subTopics.name: CQRS (Command Query Responsibility Segregation)
subTopics.description: Separating read and write operations to optimize performance, scalability, and security.

subTopics.name: Serverless Architecture
subTopics.description: Executing applications in stateless compute containers managed entirely by cloud providers.

subTopics.name: Caching Systems
subTopics.description: In-memory data stores and caching strategies to improve system read performance and latency.

subTopics.name: In-Memory Data Stores
subTopics.description: Dedicated distributed memory engines designed for ultra-low latency data access.

subTopics.name: Redis
subTopics.description: In-memory key-value data store supporting rich data structures, persistence, and pub/sub.

subTopics.name: Memcached
subTopics.description: High-performance, multithreaded in-memory key-value cache designed for string-based data storage.

subTopics.name: Caching Strategies
subTopics.description: Application and database synchronization access patterns.

subTopics.name: Cache-Aside (Lazy Loading)
subTopics.description: Application reads from cache first; if missing, reads from DB and populates cache.

subTopics.name: Write-Through
subTopics.description: Data is written to the cache and the backing database synchronously.

subTopics.name: Write-Behind (Write-Back)
subTopics.description: Data is written to the cache immediately and asynchronously batched to the database.

subTopics.name: Refresh-Ahead
subTopics.description: Cache automatically refreshes hot entries before they expire.

subTopics.name: Cache Eviction & Invalidation
subTopics.description: Algorithms and rules for managing capacity limits and data freshness.

subTopics.name: LRU (Least Recently Used)
subTopics.description: Evicts the items that have not been accessed for the longest period of time.

subTopics.name: LFU (Least Frequently Used)
subTopics.description: Evicts the items that have the lowest access frequency.

subTopics.name: TTL (Time-To-Live)
subTopics.description: Automatically invalidates and purges keys after a designated duration.

subTopics.name: Cache Invalidation & Thundering Herd
subTopics.description: Mitigating stale data, cache breakdown, penetration, and thundering herd stampedes.

subTopics.name: Data Management & Storage
subTopics.description: Database paradigms, scaling techniques, and transaction consistency models.

subTopics.name: Database Paradigms
subTopics.description: Structural models and data organization across storage types.

subTopics.name: Relational Databases (RDBMS)
subTopics.description: Structured tables, foreign keys, schema constraints, and normalized models.

subTopics.name: NoSQL Document Stores
subTopics.description: Flexible semi-structured JSON/BSON storage systems like MongoDB.

subTopics.name: NoSQL Key-Value & Column Stores
subTopics.description: High-throughput horizontally partitioned storage such as DynamoDB and Cassandra.

subTopics.name: Database Scaling Techniques
subTopics.description: Approaches for scaling database reads, writes, and capacity across nodes.

subTopics.name: Database Sharding
subTopics.description: Horizontal partitioning of database rows across multiple autonomous machines.

subTopics.name: Read Replicas & Replication
subTopics.description: Distributing read traffic using asynchronous or synchronous primary-replica copies.

subTopics.name: Partitioning Strategies
subTopics.description: Range-based, hash-based, and list-based table partitioning.

subTopics.name: Consistency & Transactions
subTopics.description: Correctness guarantees in single-node and distributed systems.

subTopics.name: ACID Properties & Isolation Levels
subTopics.description: Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation (Read Uncommitted to Serializable), and Durability.

subTopics.name: CAP & PACELC Theorems
subTopics.description: Fundamental trade-offs between Consistency, Availability, Partition tolerance, and Latency.

subTopics.name: Distributed Transactions (2PC & Saga)
subTopics.description: Managing cross-service transactions using Two-Phase Commit or choreographed/orchestrated Sagas.

subTopics.name: Asynchronous Communication
subTopics.description: Decoupled messaging systems, brokers, and event pipelines.

subTopics.name: Message Brokers & Queues
subTopics.description: Point-to-point and worker queue mechanisms for decoupled processing.

subTopics.name: RabbitMQ
subTopics.description: AMQP-based broker emphasizing routing flexibility, exchanges, and guaranteed delivery.

subTopics.name: Apache Kafka
subTopics.description: High-throughput append-only distributed commit log and event streaming platform.

subTopics.name: Messaging Paradigms & Semantics
subTopics.description: Delivery guarantees and consumption models.

subTopics.name: Publish-Subscribe (Pub/Sub)
subTopics.description: Broadcasting messages to multiple independent consumer subscriptions.

subTopics.name: Delivery Semantics
subTopics.description: Trade-offs and implementations of At-Most-Once, At-Least-Once, and Exactly-Once processing.

subTopics.name: Event Streaming & Consumer Groups
subTopics.description: Partitioned ordered reads and horizontal consumer scale-out in stream processing.

subTopics.name: Security & Identity
subTopics.description: Protocols and standards for system security, user identity, and data protection.

subTopics.name: Authentication & Authorization
subTopics.description: Verifying user identity and enforcing granular permission boundaries.

subTopics.name: OAuth 2.0 & OpenID Connect (OIDC)
subTopics.description: Delegated authorization flows, identity verification, and scopes.

subTopics.name: JSON Web Tokens (JWT)
subTopics.description: Stateless claims-based tokens with cryptographic signing and verification.

subTopics.name: Role-Based & Attribute-Based Access Control (RBAC/ABAC)
subTopics.description: Access policy enforcement models based on roles, groups, and contextual attributes.

subTopics.name: Data Protection & API Defense
subTopics.description: Safeguarding communication channels, endpoints, and stored information.

subTopics.name: Encryption (At-Rest & In-Transit)
subTopics.description: Securing data over the wire with TLS/mTLS and on disk using AES encryption.

subTopics.name: API Security & Rate Limiting
subTopics.description: Throttling, Token Bucket algorithms, CORS, CSRF, and WAF protection.

subTopics.name: Monitoring & Observability
subTopics.description: Tools and practices to track, diagnose, and maintain distributed system health.

subTopics.name: Metrics & Dashboards
subTopics.description: Time-series measurement of system counters, gauges, latencies, and saturation.

subTopics.name: Prometheus
subTopics.description: Pull-based time-series database and alerting engine using PromQL.

subTopics.name: Grafana
subTopics.description: Visualization platform to build interactive operational and business dashboards.

subTopics.name: Distributed Tracing
subTopics.description: End-to-end request propagation across asynchronous distributed services.

subTopics.name: OpenTelemetry & Jaeger
subTopics.description: Vendor-agnostic instrumentation APIs, spans, trace context propagation, and Jaeger UI.

subTopics.name: Centralized Logging
subTopics.description: Aggregation, indexing, and search of structured log output across clusters.

subTopics.name: ELK / OpenSearch Stack
subTopics.description: Logstash/Fluentd collection, Elasticsearch indexing, and Kibana log exploration.

name: SQL
description: Comprehensive SQL interview preparation covering SQL fundamentals, joins, aggregation, subqueries, correlated subqueries, window functions, and Common Table Expressions (CTEs).

subTopics.name: SQL Fundamentals
subTopics.description: Core SQL concepts and query-building fundamentals required for working with relational databases.

subTopics.name: SELECT
subTopics.description: Retrieving columns and records from database tables using SELECT queries.

subTopics.name: DISTINCT
subTopics.description: Removing duplicate rows from query results using DISTINCT.

subTopics.name: WHERE
subTopics.description: Filtering rows based on specified conditions.

subTopics.name: ORDER BY
subTopics.description: Sorting query results in ascending or descending order.

subTopics.name: LIMIT
subTopics.description: Restricting the number of rows returned by a query.

subTopics.name: Aliases
subTopics.description: Using aliases for columns and tables to make SQL queries shorter and easier to understand.

subTopics.name: LIKE
subTopics.description: Pattern matching and filtering string values using LIKE.

subTopics.name: IN
subTopics.description: Checking whether a value belongs to a specified set of values.

subTopics.name: BETWEEN
subTopics.description: Filtering values within an inclusive range.

subTopics.name: NULL Handling
subTopics.description: Understanding NULL values and filtering records involving NULL.

subTopics.name: SQL Command Categories
subTopics.description: Classification of SQL commands based on their purpose.

subTopics.name: DDL
subTopics.description: Data Definition Language commands used to define and modify database structures.

subTopics.name: DML
subTopics.description: Data Manipulation Language commands used to insert, update, and delete data.

subTopics.name: DQL
subTopics.description: Data Query Language used to retrieve data from databases.

subTopics.name: DCL
subTopics.description: Data Control Language used to manage database permissions and access.

subTopics.name: TCL
subTopics.description: Transaction Control Language used to manage database transactions.

subTopics.name: SQL Query Execution Order
subTopics.description: Understanding the logical order in which SQL query clauses are processed.

subTopics.name: FROM
subTopics.description: Identifies the source table or tables from which data is retrieved.

subTopics.name: JOIN and ON
subTopics.description: Combines related rows from multiple tables using join conditions.

subTopics.name: WHERE
subTopics.description: Filters individual rows before grouping and aggregation.

subTopics.name: GROUP BY
subTopics.description: Groups rows based on one or more columns for aggregation.

subTopics.name: HAVING
subTopics.description: Filters grouped results after aggregation.

subTopics.name: SELECT
subTopics.description: Determines the columns and expressions returned in the final result.

subTopics.name: DISTINCT
subTopics.description: Removes duplicate rows from the selected result.

subTopics.name: ORDER BY
subTopics.description: Sorts the final query result.

subTopics.name: LIMIT
subTopics.description: Restricts the number of rows returned.

subTopics.name: Joins
subTopics.description: Combining data from multiple tables using relationships between columns.

subTopics.name: INNER JOIN
subTopics.description: Returns rows where matching records exist in both joined tables.

subTopics.name: LEFT JOIN
subTopics.description: Returns all rows from the left table and matching rows from the right table.

subTopics.name: SELF JOIN
subTopics.description: Joining a table with itself, commonly used for employee-manager relationships.

subTopics.name: JOIN Conditions
subTopics.description: Using ON conditions to correctly relate rows between tables.

subTopics.name: Aggregate Functions
subTopics.description: Calculating summary values across groups or sets of rows.

subTopics.name: COUNT
subTopics.description: Counts rows or non-null values.

subTopics.name: AVG
subTopics.description: Calculates the average value of a numeric column.

subTopics.name: MAX
subTopics.description: Finds the maximum value within a set of rows.

subTopics.name: MIN
subTopics.description: Finds the minimum value within a set of rows.

subTopics.name: GROUP BY
subTopics.description: Groups rows so aggregate functions can be applied independently to each group.

subTopics.name: HAVING
subTopics.description: Filters groups based on aggregate conditions.

subTopics.name: Subqueries
subTopics.description: Using one SQL query inside another query to solve multi-step filtering and comparison problems.

subTopics.name: Basic Subqueries
subTopics.description: Using a nested query to provide a value or result set to an outer query.

subTopics.name: Scalar Subqueries
subTopics.description: Using a subquery that returns a single value for comparison in an outer query.

subTopics.name: Correlated Subqueries
subTopics.description: Subqueries that reference a column from the outer query and are evaluated relative to each outer row.

subTopics.name: Highest Salary Per Department
subTopics.description: Finding employees whose salary equals the maximum salary within their own department.

subTopics.name: Lowest Salary Per Department
subTopics.description: Finding employees whose salary equals the minimum salary within their own department.

subTopics.name: Above Department Average
subTopics.description: Finding employees whose salary is greater than the average salary of their own department.

subTopics.name: Second Highest Per Department
subTopics.description: Finding the second-highest distinct salary within each department using correlated subqueries.

subTopics.name: Salary Compared With Manager
subTopics.description: Comparing an employee's salary with the salary of their manager.

subTopics.name: Manager Team Average
subTopics.description: Comparing an employee's salary with the average salary of employees sharing the same manager.

subTopics.name: EXISTS
subTopics.description: Testing whether a correlated subquery returns at least one matching row.

subTopics.name: NOT EXISTS
subTopics.description: Testing whether a correlated subquery returns no matching rows.

subTopics.name: ANY
subTopics.description: Comparing a value against at least one value returned by a subquery.

subTopics.name: ALL
subTopics.description: Comparing a value against every value returned by a subquery.

subTopics.name: Duplicate Detection
subTopics.description: Finding employees with duplicate salaries while excluding the current employee from the comparison.

subTopics.name: Unique Values Within Group
subTopics.description: Finding employees whose salary occurs only once within their department.

subTopics.name: Window Functions
subTopics.description: Performing calculations across related rows while preserving individual rows in the result.

subTopics.name: PARTITION BY
subTopics.description: Divides rows into logical groups for window calculations without collapsing the rows.

subTopics.name: Window ORDER BY
subTopics.description: Defines the ordering of rows inside each window partition.

subTopics.name: ROW_NUMBER
subTopics.description: Assigns a unique sequential number to each row within a window partition.

subTopics.name: RANK
subTopics.description: Assigns the same rank to tied values while leaving gaps after ties.

subTopics.name: DENSE_RANK
subTopics.description: Assigns the same rank to tied values without leaving gaps after ties.

subTopics.name: SUM OVER
subTopics.description: Calculating totals and running totals using SUM as a window function.

subTopics.name: Department Total
subTopics.description: Calculating the total salary for each department while keeping every employee row.

subTopics.name: Running Total
subTopics.description: Calculating cumulative salary values according to a defined row ordering.

subTopics.name: AVG OVER
subTopics.description: Calculating averages across window partitions without collapsing individual rows.

subTopics.name: Department Average
subTopics.description: Adding the department's average salary to every employee row.

subTopics.name: Moving Average
subTopics.description: Calculating an average over a limited number of preceding rows and the current row.

subTopics.name: LAG
subTopics.description: Accessing a value from a previous row within an ordered window.

subTopics.name: Previous Salary
subTopics.description: Retrieving the previous employee's salary within the same department.

subTopics.name: Salary Difference
subTopics.description: Comparing the current employee's salary with the previous employee's salary.

subTopics.name: LEAD
subTopics.description: Accessing a value from the next row within an ordered window.

subTopics.name: Next Salary
subTopics.description: Retrieving the next employee's salary within the same department.

subTopics.name: Window Frames
subTopics.description: Controlling exactly which rows are included in a window calculation.

subTopics.name: UNBOUNDED PRECEDING
subTopics.description: Starts the window frame from the first row of the partition.

subTopics.name: CURRENT ROW
subTopics.description: Defines the current row as the end or starting point of a window frame.

subTopics.name: N PRECEDING
subTopics.description: Includes a specified number of rows before the current row.

subTopics.name: ROWS BETWEEN
subTopics.description: Defines a row-based window frame for calculations such as running totals and moving averages.

subTopics.name: Top N Per Group
subTopics.description: Finding the top employees within each department using ranking window functions.

subTopics.name: Second Highest Per Group
subTopics.description: Finding the second-highest distinct salary per department using DENSE_RANK.

subTopics.name: Window Function With Subquery
subTopics.description: Using a subquery to filter results based on a calculated window-function alias.

subTopics.name: Common Table Expressions (CTE)
subTopics.description: Using named temporary query results to structure complex SQL queries into readable and reusable logical steps.

subTopics.name: CTE Fundamentals
subTopics.description: Understanding the WITH clause and defining a named temporary result set.

subTopics.name: Basic CTE
subTopics.description: Creating a CTE and using it in the main SELECT query.

subTopics.name: CTE With Aggregation
subTopics.description: Using GROUP BY and aggregate functions inside a CTE.

subTopics.name: CTE With HAVING
subTopics.description: Filtering aggregated groups inside a CTE using HAVING.

subTopics.name: CTE With Window Functions
subTopics.description: Combining CTEs with window functions such as DENSE_RANK for multi-step queries.

subTopics.name: Multiple CTEs
subTopics.description: Defining multiple CTEs in a single WITH clause and combining their results.

subTopics.name: CTE With JOIN
subTopics.description: Joining a CTE with the original table or another CTE to solve multi-step problems.

subTopics.name: CTE vs Subquery
subTopics.description: Understanding when a named CTE provides better readability and structure than nested subqueries.

subTopics.name: Interview Problem-Solving Patterns
subTopics.description: Practical SQL patterns repeatedly used in interview questions and real-world query development.

subTopics.name: Highest Salary
subTopics.description: Finding the highest salary globally or within each department.

subTopics.name: Second Highest Salary
subTopics.description: Finding the second-highest salary using subqueries and ranking techniques.

subTopics.name: Highest Salary Per Department
subTopics.description: Finding all employees tied for the highest salary in each department.

subTopics.name: Second Highest Salary Per Department
subTopics.description: Finding employees with the second-highest distinct salary in each department.

subTopics.name: Above Department Average
subTopics.description: Finding employees earning more than their department's average salary.
